answer: Sybil resistance employs a hardware-attested identity coupled with a resource burn. Each AI agent requires a unique, verifiable hardware attestation. Furthermore, to gain full network privileges, agents must burn a scarce computational "thread" token, expensive to acquire. This acquisition might involve a dedicated "raven" cryptographic computation or a substantial "copper" resource deposit. The prohibitive, non-linear cost per attested identity, proportional to physical hardware and resource burn, makes large-scale Sybil attacks economically infeasible.
